text:
maria: FYI ran the compact-algo experiments on the hetero hosts this morning. results are... weird.
kevin: weird how? numbers?
maria: tail latency spikes on sparse workloads when compact runs concurrently with prefetch. p95/99 up ~2-3x for ~120s window. average fine.
oliver: do you have traces? maybe compactor is starving the prefetch threads or stealing cpu cycles.
maria: attached snippets from perf/trace:

```
compact_cycle: 4500ms loop
prefetch_workers: 8 -> stalled for 90-110ms bursts
cpu % steal jumps 12% during compact
```

maria: also saw alignment churn: many small move ops logged which cause mutex contention.
kevin: hmm. did you test with compact rate-limiting enabled? we have the knob `compact.max_moves_per_sec`.
maria: yes tried 10k -> still spike. tried 1k -> lower spike but still visible. zeroing compaction removes spike.
anika: could be allocator fragmentation pattern triggering extra page pin/unpin across NUMA. what's the alloc shape?
maria: workload is long-running sparse embedding serving: many 64B-1KB allocations, rare large buffers. hotset is tiny but spread across tenants.
oliver: that explains it. compactor moves lots of tiny objects -> metadata updates and cross-node bounce. two ideas: 1) micro-compact: prefer in-place slab consolidation (coalesce slots without move) 2) cooperative compaction: yield to prefetch/serving threads and spread work over longer wall time.
kevin: +1 on cooperative. maybe integrate with admission: compactor checks `serve_slo_margin` and pauses if margin < 10%.
anika: re: micro-compact, we need a new API on the allocator to attempt local coalesce without relocation. that's a moderate refactor but could be cheap.
maria: experiment logs from host B (with cpulimit on compactor to 20%): p99 normalized to baseline within 10% and throughput steady. so rate-limiting helps, but throughput of compaction is too slow to actually mitigate fragmentation over time.
kevin: tradeoff then: aggressive compaction reduces long-term frag but causes transient SLO regressions; throttled compaction keeps SLOs but allows frag growth.
oliver: can we do hybrid: fast background compacts during low qps windows + incremental cooperative compaction during normal operation? schedule aligned to tenant quiet windows?
anika: tenant-awareness would need compaction metadata per-tenant and a scheduler. that ties into our reservation/lease systems. bigger change.
maria: short term proposal: ship adaptive backoff: compactor monitors p99 and `serve_slo_margin` and increases sleep when p99 > target*1.1. fallback: if frag percent > threshold, escalate to maintenance window compaction (manual).
kevin: make sure we add observability: compaction cycles, moves/sec, avg move size, CPU% and p99 overlay. we should be able to pivot quickly.
anika: agreed. also add a small experiment to implement local-coalesce proof-of-concept in allocator (no cross-page moves) and benchmark.
oliver: can I own the POC? should be a small patch to slab manager. will pair with you, anika.
maria: thanks. i'll push the adaptive backoff PR tomorrow, include the telemetry.
ci-bot: build queued for branch: feature/compact-adaptive-backoff (#3721). tests: unit x124, integration x12.
kevin: nice. timeline?
maria: PR by EOD tomorrow, small rollout: canary on non-prod racks, monitor p99 for 24h, then gradual.
anika: i'll schedule allocator PoC for next sprint.
oliver: typo nit: call the flag `compaction.slo_backoff_ratio` not margin.
maria: noted. will update. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks team. let's document the experiment in the runbook and add a dashboard for quick toggles.
